feed.title: Long Horizon Notes

bullets: Macro is mostly about not being on the wrong side of a regime change — the second order effect is the part most people miss.
Risk you can articulate is risk you can manage; once internalized, the rest of the decisions get easier.
Reliability of expectations is the underrated piece of macro analysis — it determines which trade offs you're making.
The dollar is a system, not a price — ignoring that leads to rebuilding it from scratch a year later.
Outside of Vanguard-class tooling, the failure mode is harder to spot, making the framing matter because it tells you which trade offs you're making.
Systems thinking applies to macro policy — the trade offs around it crosscut everything covered in the conversation.
A practical next step is to pick one of the covered ideas and run it for two weeks — the rest is iteration.
